chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from 'Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Silk and silk brocade are not suitable for wearing; as for their sale, there is no objection to it.

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell silk if men cannot wear it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the distinction between the prohibition of wearing silk and brocade for men and the permissibility of their trade, reflecting the juristic principle that the utility of an item does not negate its commercial validity. It highlights the nuanced approach of Shia fiqh in separating ritual purity and modesty regulations from economic transactions, ensuring that markets for luxury goods remain active despite specific usage restrictions.
